quests.instruction: Which two small words make the compound word “playground”?
quests.hint: A compound word is two words joined together.
quests.explanation: “Playground” is play + ground. Each part keeps its meaning.
quests.funFact: Compound words are two words joined together to make a new word with a new meaning.

quests.instruction: Which word is a compound word?
quests.hint: Look for a word that can be split into two real words.
quests.explanation: “Rainbow” is rain + bow. “Rabbit” and “rainy” cannot be split into two whole words.

quests.instruction: Join “back” and “pack”. Which word do you make?
quests.hint: Keep the words in order.
quests.explanation: “Back” + “pack” makes “backpack”. The order of the two words matters.

quests.instruction: Which word is made of /s/ /u/ /n/ + /sh/ /ī/ /n/?
quests.hint: Blend the two chunks. The second chunk has a digraph.
quests.explanation: “Sun” + “shine” makes “sunshine”. The second chunk has the digraph sh and long i.
quests.funFact: Sunshine, sunset and sunflower are all compound words that start with sun.

quests.instruction: Which compound word has three syllables?
quests.hint: Break each word into syllables.
quests.explanation: “Butterfly” divides but-ter-fly. “Football” and “sunset” have two syllables.

quests.instruction: What are the two words in “pancake”?
quests.hint: Look for two words you know.
quests.explanation: “Pancake” is pan + cake. Each word is a CVC or silent-e word you know.

quests.instruction: Words like “table” and “candle” end with a consonant plus le. How many syllables does “candle” have?
quests.hint: Clap as you say can-dle.
quests.explanation: “Candle” has 2 syllables: can-dle. The last syllable is consonant + le.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the syllable -le?
quests.hint: Find the word whose ending looks like the end of table.
quests.explanation: “Puzzle” ends with le, so it divides puz-zle.

quests.instruction: Which word divides as lit-tle?
quests.hint: Say it in chunks and check the last syllable.
quests.explanation: “Little” divides lit-tle. “Litter” ends with er and “lit” has one syllable.
quests.funFact: The last syllable in many words, such as apple, bottle and gentle, is a consonant followed by le.

quests.instruction: The ending -tion says /shun/. Which word ends with /shun/?
quests.hint: Say each word. Which one ends with the sound sh-un?
quests.explanation: “Nation” ends with -tion, which says /shun/.
quests.funFact: Many -tion words, like nation, station and action, come from Latin.

quests.instruction: The ending -tion counts as one beat. How many syllables does “vacation” have?
quests.hint: Clap the beats and remember that -tion is one syllable.
quests.explanation: “Vacation” has 3 syllables: va-ca-tion.

quests.instruction: Which word has the /shun/ ending?
quests.hint: Look at the last four letters.
quests.explanation: “Action” ends with -tion. “Acting” ends with -ing and “active” ends with -ive.

quests.instruction: Break “banana” into syllables.
quests.hint: Clap the word as you say it slowly.
quests.explanation: “Banana” has three syllables: ba-na-na.
quests.funFact: In banana, two of the three syllables sound exactly the same: na and na.

quests.instruction: Read the syllables: “tor” + “na” + “do”. Which word do they make?
quests.hint: Blend all three chunks together.
quests.explanation: “Tor” + “na” + “do” makes “tornado”. The first syllable has /or/.

quests.instruction: Which word is split into syllables correctly?
quests.hint: Say the word slowly and tap each beat.
quests.explanation: “Umbrella” divides um-brel-la, with three beats.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same -ight pattern as “flight”?
quests.hint: Look for the letters igh in the word.
quests.explanation: “Tonight” has the igh pattern, just like “flight”.
quests.funFact: Tonight, flight, right, bright and fight share the -ight pattern.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same /ar/ spelling as “garden”?
quests.hint: Look for the letters ar.
quests.explanation: “Market” has ar, like “garden”. “Monster” and “motor” have different vowel sounds.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same vowel team as “raindrop”?
quests.hint: Look for the letters ai.
quests.explanation: “Painted” has ai like “raindrop”. “Rabbit” and “pencil” have short vowels.

quests.instruction: Chunk the word “fantastic”. Which chunks are right?
quests.hint: Divide between the consonants in the middle.
quests.explanation: “Fantastic” divides fan-tas-tic. Each chunk has one vowel sound.
quests.funFact: Fantastic is a long word, but it is easy to read in three small chunks.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same last syllable as “window”?
quests.hint: Say the last chunk of each word and compare it with window.
quests.explanation: “Window” and “pillow” both end with low, where ow says long o.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same first syllable as “market”?
quests.hint: Say the first chunk of market.
quests.explanation: “Market” and “marble” both start with mar, which has an r-controlled vowel.

quests.instruction: Which word has a digraph in its first syllable?
quests.hint: Look at the first two letters.
quests.explanation: “Chicken” starts with ch, a digraph, in chick-en.
quests.funFact: Chicken has two digraphs: ch at the start and ck in the middle, each making one sound.

quests.instruction: Which word has a blend in the second syllable?
quests.hint: Look at the second chunk of each word.
quests.explanation: “Hamster” divides ham-ster, and ster starts with the blend st.

quests.instruction: “Sunshine” is two words joined together. How many sounds does it have in total?
quests.hint: Count carefully. The sh is one sound and the e is silent.
quests.explanation: “Sunshine” has 6 sounds: /s/ /u/ /n/ /sh/ /ī/ /n/.

quests.instruction: Which word has a vowel team in its first syllable?
quests.hint: Look at the first chunk of each word.
quests.explanation: “Rainbow” starts with ai in rain. “Rabbit” and “napkin” start with short vowels.
quests.funFact: Rainbow has two vowel teams: ai in rain and ow in bow.

quests.instruction: Which word has an r-controlled vowel in the first syllable?
quests.hint: Look for the letters ar, or, er, ir or ur.
quests.explanation: “Garden” starts with gar, with /ar/. “Giraffe” and “gather” do not have an r-controlled first syllable.

quests.instruction: Which word has the long a sound in its first syllable?
quests.hint: Divide each word and check the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Paper” divides pa-per, an open syllable, so a says its name.

quests.instruction: Clap “watermelon” slowly. How many syllables is it?
quests.hint: Say it in big chunks and clap each chunk.
quests.explanation: “Watermelon” has 4 syllables: wa-ter-mel-on.
quests.funFact: Watermelon is built from two smaller words, water and melon.

quests.instruction: Which shows “pencil” split into syllables the right way?
quests.hint: Find the two consonants in the middle of pencil.
quests.explanation: “Pencil” divides pen-cil.

quests.instruction: Which compound word has an r-controlled vowel in its first word?
quests.hint: Look at the first word of each compound.
quests.explanation: “Starfish” starts with star, which has /ar/. “Sunfish” and “goldfish” do not.
